summary: Tested new PUT /api/articles/{id} endpoint plus full regression of auth, articles CRUD, likes, comments, and CORS. All 25 executed tests passed; 3 skipped were guard-skips that depended on at least one seeded article (collection was intentionally cleared, as documented).
tests_added_for_put_endpoint: test_update_owner_partial_title_only (partial update preserves other fields, GET-verified)
test_update_admin_can_edit_any_article (admin edits another teacher's article, GET-verified)

regression_results.auth: register / login / me / logout / wrong-password / duplicate-email all PASS; httpOnly cookie set & cleared correctly
regression_results.articles_crud: list / create / get / delete / non-owner-403 / admin-can-delete / 404 all PASS
regression_results.likes: toggle PASS; like-requires-auth SKIPPED (no seeded articles to target with anonymous client)
regression_results.comments: add+delete PASS; delete-other-user-403 PASS; list/add-requires-auth SKIPPED (no seeded articles)

critical_code_review_comments: PUT /api/articles/{id} correctly enforces owner-or-admin authorization, supports partial updates, sets updated_at timestamp, strips _id, and re-uses enrich_article for response shape.
ArticleUpdate model uses Optional fields with the same min_length/max_length constraints as ArticleCreate -> consistent validation.
Minor: response_model=ArticleOut is great. Consider also returning 404 with consistent Arabic message (already done).
Minor (pre-existing, not blocking): server.py uses deprecated FastAPI on_event('startup'/'shutdown') hooks; migrate to lifespan context for FastAPI >=0.95.
Minor: list_comments has no auth dependency, so liked_by_me-style personalization is N/A; consistent with current spec.
